judged_text: The Salesforce token refresh now runs unconditionally inside the connection-building path on every CalendarService construction, adding a network round-trip to login.salesforce.com plus a credential-table write per service instantiation even when credential sharing is disabled. Every calendar read/write for Salesforce users pays an extra provider round-trip and DB write on each service construction (previously jsforce refreshed lazily on demand), multiplying provider rate-limit pressure and credential-row churn under booking load.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token HTTP call to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` plus a `prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no guard on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, and the refresh/update occur on this code path every time the service constructs/initializes its connection, which can add an extra provider round-trip and DB write per instantiation (a performance/rate-limit/DB-churn concern rather than a direct correctness defect).
